title: IELTS Listening Practice - Listening - Social Media Trends
subject: Listening

questions.q:
### Context: Rage bait: How online anger makes money - 6 Minute English

**Watch the video (or listen to the audio context provided) and answer Questions 26-40.**

![Rage bait: How online anger makes money](https://img.youtube.com/vi/JaGXfJBx0BM/mqdefault.jpg)
[Watch on YouTube](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JaGXfJBx0BM)

**Questions 26–30**
Choose the correct letter, **a**, **b**, or **c**.

26. According to the introduction, what is the main purpose of 'clickbait' headlines?
options: To grab attention and encourage reading.
To discourage people from using social media.
questions.explain: Phil states: 'Headlines like these are used to grab your attention and make you read more.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 27. What is the specific aim of 'rage bait' content?
options: To make the viewer feel angry or outraged.
questions.explain: Beth defines it: 'Rage bait is online content designed to make you angry or outraged.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 28. According to Andrea Jones, why do creators prioritize getting more views?
questions.explain: Andrea says: 'the more views they get, the more that they get paid.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 29. How does Andrea Jones characterize a marketing 'hook'?
options: It comes from a place of trust and accuracy.
It is exactly the same as clickbait.
questions.explain: Andrea states: 'a hook accurately reflects what's in that piece of content and it comes from a place of trust.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 30. In contrast to a hook, how does Andrea describe rage bait?
options: It is designed to be manipulative.
questions.explain: Andrea says: 'whereas rage baiting content is designed to be manipulative.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q:
**Questions 31–36**
Complete the sentences below. Write **NO MORE THAN TWO WORDS** for each answer.

31. Andrea Jones explains that even if engagement is negative, the creator still makes more ______.
questions.explain: Beth summarizes Andrea's point: 'the more reaction a post gets, the more money the creator makes.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 32. Dr. William Brady uses the informal term '______' to refer to people viewing content.
questions.explain: Dr. Brady asks: 'how do I get more eyeballs on my content?'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 33. To get attention, influencers often exploit specific ______ in human psychology.
questions.explain: Dr. Brady states: 'you need to exploit those biases we have in our psychology.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 34. These psychological biases are described as feelings which are often ______.
questions.explain: Phil defines biases as: 'feelings which are often unconscious.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 35. Beth notes that listening to emotions has been vital to the ______ of the human species.
questions.explain: Beth says: 'listening to our emotions has been vital to the evolution of the human species.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 36. Phil warns that by sharing outrageous content, you might be making the creator ______.
questions.explain: Phil concludes: 'while also making the creator richer.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q:
**Questions 37–40**
Match the term (**A–D**) to its definition.

A. Clickbait
B. Rage bait
C. Hook
D. Bias

37. Content designed to grab attention and make you read more, often used in headlines.
questions.explain: Phil defines clickbait: 'Headlines like these are used to grab your attention and make you read more.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 38. Marketing content that accurately reflects the post and is trustworthy.
questions.explain: Andrea says: 'a hook accurately reflects what's in that piece of content... comes from a place of trust.'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 39. An unconscious feeling for or against a certain idea or group of people.
questions.explain: Phil defines biases: 'feelings, which are often unconscious, either for or against a certain idea...'
questions.subject: Listening

questions.q: 40. Content specifically designed to provoke anger or outrage.
questions.explain: Beth states: 'Rage bait is online content designed to make you angry or outraged.'
questions.subject: Listening
